qualified_families.qualification: Legacy-successful public MetaModel chains with automatic or explicit levels through depth four, ordered base/meta sources, probability and label ports, fold test aggregation, coverage policies, branch scopes, named independent terminals, and supported source selectors run through DAG-ML PyO3/CLI with native CV, REFIT and archive replay. Native fold-local OOF may yield different scores from legacy.

The generic two-stage contract is qualified on legacy-successful Ridge, PLSRegression and RandomForestRegressor base/learner combinations, plus ElasticNet choices, nonlinear/named operators, PyTorch learner controls, source/target transforms, branches, joins, numeric gates and lambda, learner search, PyO3/CLI REFIT and archive replay. Arbitrary operator implementations form an open-ended provider compatibility surface rather than a finite feature-gap checklist. Each new operator pair needs a finite legacy oracle before a DAG refusal can be classified as a parity gap.
qualified_families.evidence: test_residual_operator_matrix.py::test_residual_public_operator_pair_cv_refit_archive; test_residual_numeric_contract.py; test_residual_composition_matrix.py; test_residual_source_concat.py; test_residual_target_preprocessing.py; test_residual_public_syntax.py; test_residual_legacy_limits.py; test_controller_inventory.py::test_residual_nested_operator_choices_select_cv_winner_and_replay

qualified_families.qualification: DAG-ML host HPO is qualified on Python RandomForest/Ridge/PyTorch, R Ridge through CLI, Octave Ridge through CLI, and Node/Chrome local Ridge through WASM workers. The real language-local oracles check fold-train IDs, native fold/OOF scores, trial selection, pruning and resume, then full-train REFIT and fresh-process or worker artifact replay with RDS/MAT or WASM artifact state. This is operator-scoped evidence; it does not imply every R/MATLAB/JS operator or proprietary MATLAB runtime is tested. Local Octave validation is not an assertion that CI provisions Octave.

documented_divergences.classification: legacy reuses global/external OOF across stacking levels and allows outer-validation labels to influence same-fold meta predictions; DAG-ML requires nested fold-local OOF and refuses when the sample universe becomes too small
documented_divergences.pipeline: 20x4 seeded regression rows, KFold(2), Ridge, ten named MetaModel(Ridge) levels with StackingConfig(max_level=10)
documented_divergences.legacy: The public run returns finite CV scores/predictions. Perturbing only one fold-0 validation target leaves the fold-0 base Ridge predictions exactly unchanged but changes fold-0 meta1 predictions by more than one unit and deeply changes meta10 predictions. Thus the legacy score is not a leakage-safe ten-level oracle.
documented_divergences.dagml: Native PyO3 detects the chain but refuses `KFold n_splits=2 exceeds sample count 1` when repeated train-only inner OOF reaches a one-row fit universe. It does not silently recycle the global OOF predictions that expose validation labels.
documented_divergences.evidence: test_dagml_metamodel_explicit_levels.py::test_ten_levels_need_more_rows_for_native_nested_oof; dag-ml fold.rs KFoldSpec::build; runtime/stacking.rs nested fold scope
documented_divergences.scope: DAG-ML runs and replays qualified chains through depth four; small-N/deep chains need more training rows for leak-free nested KFold. The legacy high-depth finite score must not be treated as a feature-parity target. Retain the strict default refusal; any unsafe legacy emulation would require an explicit, separately designed opt-in and provenance.

documented_divergences.classification: operator-specific cross-language codec and executor boundary; generic DAG-ML Raw transport is implemented
documented_divergences.legacy: A single-output fitted sklearn Ridge archive replays through legacy BundleLoader; the current public nirs4all.predict API rejects legacy bundles under the native migration policy. A legacy independent by-source archive can be written but cannot replay (separate documented divergence).
documented_divergences.dagml: PyO3 and CLI both fit Ridge, export a general .n4a with one Python joblib host artifact, and replay it through public nirs4all.predict; PyTorch customizable_decon also has Python-host archive replay tests on both mechanisms. This host archive has no portable Raw package reference. DAG-ML Core, C, WASM, PyO3 and persistent CLI already transport signed Raw bytes with export/hydrate/release; a Methods PLS N4MM codec proves cross-language replay. The generic byte protocol cannot define sklearn or arbitrary Python object inference in C/Rust/WASM.
documented_divergences.evidence: test_python_host_archive_boundary.py (legacy BundleLoader and DAG PyO3/CLI Ridge replay plus host archive shape); test_dagml_torch_models.py:test_builtin_customizable_decon_run_export_replay; test_dagml_cli_full_train.py:test_legacy_by_source_auto_archive_has_no_replayable_model; dag-ml-cli cli_replays_portable_methods_pls_payload_in_fresh_process; dag-ml core/C/WASM/PyO3 Raw package and persistent_process_controller_roundtrips_portable_raw_artifact_frames
documented_divergences.proposed_contract: Keep arbitrary Python estimators as explicit Python-host artifacts. To make a particular operator portable, define a versioned language-neutral codec for its fitted state and matching inference controller in each target language, then prove fresh-process and cross-language replay. Do not label joblib/cloudpickle bytes Raw portable merely because the generic transport accepts bytes.
documented_divergences.scope: The generic DAG-ML Raw bytes protocol already spans Core, C, WASM, PyO3 and CLI. Python joblib model inference is a Python operator capability; another language needs its own versioned estimator codec and executor for that specific operator. The user requires generic pipeline parity across languages at the operator boundary, not portable inference for arbitrary Python objects.

documented_divergences.classification: legacy residual training reuses external OOF predictions while DAG-ML uses nested OOF within each outer training fold
documented_divergences.pipeline: 20 train and 4 test rows, KFold(2) -> y_processing(StandardScaler) -> branch(two Ridge models) -> merge(predictions) -> ResidualModel(base=PLSRegression(2), learner=Ridge, gate=auto)
documented_divergences.control: On the identical rows, splitter, target scaler and residual model without the prediction join, legacy and DAG-ML CV RMSE are 1.7183788837956848 and 1.7183788542509857.
documented_divergences.evidence: test_residual_capacity_policy.py:test_residual_prediction_join_pls_capacity_refit_and_replay verifies both public mechanisms and archive replay; dag-ml fold.rs:outer_oof_is_not_safe_training_evidence_for_an_outer_fold_meta_model proves external OOF training would use current outer-validation labels; residual_model.py:execute consumes external OOF; runtime/stacking.rs:replace_nested_stacking_fit_cv_inputs uses inner OOF
documented_divergences.scope: The controlled no-join scores agree to 3e-8, so target scaling alone does not explain the joined-score gap. With the join, legacy reuses outer OOF base predictions that were fit using the current fold's validation labels; DAG-ML refits within the outer train and scores its held-out fold. The CV scores therefore describe different fit scopes and need not match. This evidence does not promise numerical convergence of every PLS fit or identify every source of a score difference in other datasets.

documented_divergences.classification: legacy passes each CV validation fold to AutoGluon as tuning_data
documented_divergences.evidence: autogluon_model.py:_train_model; test_dagml_autogluon_model.py; test_dagml_autogluon_native.py against real AutoGluon 1.6.1; direct TabularPredictor two-scope control on the same StratifiedKFold rows
documented_divergences.scope: The DAG-ML host adapter trains AutoGluon on fold-train rows only and lets AutoGluon select its internal holdout. Giving the CV validation labels to the operator would leak the evaluation fold into fitting. On one 100-row binary LightGBM case, public legacy scored 0.919 versus DAG-ML 0.500. A direct AutoGluon 1.6.1 control on those same folds predicted only class 1 with internal holdout (balanced accuracy 0.500 in each fold), but predicted both classes when given the CV validation rows as tuning_data (balanced accuracy 0.941 and 0.897). This explains this case's score gap and does not make legacy validation leakage a target contract.

documented_divergences.scope: The public legacy run raises AttributeError on set.__dict__ in component_serialization._changed_kwargs. The equivalent source_models=all path is supported by DAG-ML, but this selector itself has no successful legacy oracle and the DAG adapter keeps it unsupported.

documented_divergences.classification: legacy MetaModel finetune_space grid trials score infinity after a nested parameter is sent to the inner estimator
documented_divergences.pipeline: KFold(2), Ridge, MetaModel(Ridge, finetune_space={model__alpha:[0.1,0.2], n_trials:2, sampler:grid})
documented_divergences.scope: Both Optuna trials complete with value infinity because Ridge.set_params receives model={alpha:...}; the public run can still report a finite CV score and may fit a candidate alpha afterward, which does not validate the trials. DAG-ML rejects MetaModel finetune_space until a native whole-stack nested search and a working legacy tuning oracle exist.
